title: LabVIEW to Python, at fleet scale
subtitle: Walkthrough of this repository: what was built, which skill to run when, exactly how, and what each step proves. Offline, on Devin Desktop, no cloud.
footer: Synthetic and public open-source example data only. No customer system, program, or site.

slides.title: Part 1. What you are holding
This repository in one slide
bullets: A library of 15 ready-to-run Devin Desktop skills (slash commands) plus small Python tools they call
Everything runs on a laptop: Python 3.10+, standard library only, no network, no cloud service
Two skills carry the LabVIEW work: /vi-fleet-discovery (the whole estate) and /labview-to-python (one rig)
Three more close the loop: /track-and-report (backlog status), /exec-deck (the brief), /tour (first run)
A synthetic example system and four real public-domain-licensed VIs are included so every step can be rehearsed offline
Every number in every report comes from a tool, never typed by hand; every result lands in outputs/
slides.note: Sources: README.md, AGENTS.md, tools/check_repo.py (16 skills), tools/golden_path.py (17 stages)

slides.title: What it promises, and what it refuses to promise
left: Count and read every VI in a tree without a LabVIEW licence (lvkit, optional)
Classify each VI: port / wrap / retain / unreadable, with the evidence written next to it
Rebuild a rig's behaviour in Python from its documentation and diagram
Prove the rebuild row by row against a recording of the original rig
Track the backlog and brief leadership from the same numbers
right: "Point at the .vi, get equivalent Python." A .vi is a proprietary binary; nobody can read intent out of it
Proving timing, FPGA, Real-Time, or instrument behaviour on a laptop
A classification that replaces the recording: it orders the work, it does not prove a port
Automatic code generation as the deliverable (lvkit generate failed on 4 of 4 real VIs)

slides.title: Part 2. Before the first run
Setup, step by step (no assumptions)
bullets: 1. Copy the repository folder onto the laptop that has Devin Desktop. Nothing else is downloaded
2. Open a terminal in that folder and run: python tools/doctor.py . Expect the last line READY
3. If it says Python is too old, install Python 3.10 or newer; nothing else is required

4. Optional: lvkit (reads .vi files). Online: python3 -m pip install lvkit . Offline: an administrator runs pip download on a connected machine, copies the wheels folder, then pip install --no-index --find-links
5. Run python tools/check_repo.py once. It validates every skill, link, and test; expect OK
6. Open the folder in Devin Desktop. Skills appear as /commands in the chat box because they live in .devin/skills/
7. First time: type /tour . It checks the laptop, runs every test, and opens the example deck

slides.title: How a skill is run, every time
bullets: Type the slash command followed by its argument, for example: /vi-fleet-discovery example-system --name demo-fleet
Devin reads the SKILL.md for that command and follows its steps in order; you can read the same file
Each skill asks before it executes a tool or writes a file (the permissions block in its frontmatter). Say yes to the commands you see here
Results go to outputs/ (ignored by git). Copy anything you want to keep
Every skill names the file it produced and the file the next skill should read; hand that path over explicitly
The chain for this work is in WORKFLOWS.md, section 9; the routing table in AGENTS.md maps phrases to skills
Stuck? python tools/doctor.py again, then read the skill file. Nothing needs an account or a network

slides.title: Part 3. The end-to-end chain
Five stages, five skills, one estate
The four verdicts, in plain words
bullets: port: the VI is sequencing, maths, strings, limits, file I/O, or reporting. Python can do this; /labview-to-python rebuilds and proves it
wrap: the VI talks to hardware through a driver (DAQmx, VISA, IVI, a DLL, .NET, TestStand). Keep the VI or driver, call it from Python, port the logic around it
retain: FPGA, Real-Time, timed loops, DAQmx hardware timing, anything under an RT or FPGA target. It stays in LabVIEW; document why and move on
unreadable: the reader failed, the diagram is password protected, or lvkit is not installed. Ask the owner for the HTML export before deciding anything
Rules are applied in the order unreadable, retain, wrap, port; the first match wins and the evidence is written in the reasons column
Evidence tagged [file name only] came from the path, not the diagram. Treat it as a hint

slides.title: Stage 1. /vi-fleet-discovery: the whole estate
When to run it, and what to have ready
bullets: Run it first, before anyone promises a schedule: it answers how many VIs, what is in them, and where to start
Have a read-only copy of the folder tree. It may hold .vi, .lvproj, .lvlib, .lvclass, TestStand .seq, exported HTML, and recordings; all are picked up
Check python tools/doctor.py: the Optional tools row says whether lvkit is installed. Without it, VIs are listed but not read
Decide a label per run (--name lab-a). Re-running with the same label after a sprint rewrites the inventory (sha256 shows what changed) and merges the backlog: ids and statuses survive
For a huge tree, smoke-test with --limit 200 first, then run per project folder; expect about one second per VI with lvkit
The scanner only reads. lvkit writes a cache under the user's home folder, never into the tree

slides.title: Exactly how to run it
bullets: In Devin Desktop: /vi-fleet-discovery <path to the tree> --name <label>
Or in a terminal: python tools/vi_fleet_scan.py <tree> --name <label> --top 30
Rehearsal on the shipped example: python tools/vi_fleet_scan.py example-system --name demo-fleet
Then: python tools/tracker_report.py --file outputs/demo-fleet-migration-backlog.json (the backlog, ranked)
Then open outputs/demo-fleet-fleet-inventory.csv in any spreadsheet and sort by priority, largest first
Self-test at any time: python tools/vi_fleet_scan.py --check compares a fresh scan of the example with the checked-in expected CSV
Options: --jobs 4 (parallel, after a first serial run), --no-index (skip the call graph), --json (summary to stdout)

slides.title: With lvkit and without: what changes
left: Every VI's connector pane, structures, SubVIs, primitives, unresolved mappings, health flags
Call graph: callers_count and impact_score from lvkit index + query
Verdicts come from the diagram; reasons cite nodes by name
About one second per VI; corrupt files become one unreadable row each
right: Every VI still listed with size, hash, project file, target, sequences, missing inputs
Verdict unreadable with reason lvkit absent, unless the name or .lvproj target says retain or wrap
The doctor row and the summary say lvkit absent in those words

slides.title: Nuances at a hundred thousand VIs
bullets: Time: two reader calls per file, about a second in all. Plan a day of machine time per hundred thousand VIs; run per lab, overnight, --name per run
Failures are isolated: lvkit stops at the first corrupt file when given a folder, so the scanner calls it per file and keeps going
lvkit index covers the nearest enclosing .git or .lvkit root, which can be larger than the tree; the summary note says how many VIs it covered
Password-protected diagrams and VIs saved without a diagram stay unreadable until the owner supplies the export
TestStand .seq files are binary by default; only XML or INI forms are read. Binary ones are listed with a conversion note
Verdicts are static evidence; the reader column records the lvkit version, and the checked-in expected CSV is tied to 0.8.4

slides.title: Stage 2. Choose where to start
Picking the first sprint from the CSV
bullets: Sort by priority, largest first: it rewards many callers, a recording beside the VI, exported docs, and low complexity
Take the first ten port rows whose owner can produce a recording of one real run. Without a recording nothing can be proven
Prefer shared utility VIs (high callers_count): one port retires work in every caller
Skip retain entirely; skip unreadable until the export or password arrives; queue wrap rows behind the port rows that use them
Write outputs/<name>-fleet-report.md: counts from the summary JSON, the top candidates with reasons, the asks, and the sentence that classification is static evidence
Ask Devin to draft it: Read outputs/<name>-fleet-inventory.csv and write the fleet report: counts, top ten port candidates with reasons, what is missing
Hand the report and the backlog to Stage 3 and Stage 4

slides.title: Stage 3. /labview-to-python: one rig at a time
When to run it, and what to gather first
bullets: Run it once per candidate VI, in backlog order, after Stage 2 named the rig and its recording
Best input: LabVIEW's own HTML export (File > Print > HTML, VI documentation with block diagram). Ask the owner; it needs LabVIEW once
Next best: front-panel and block-diagram screenshots, one per case-structure frame; a VI Analyzer report; the .lvproj
TestStand .seq (XML) or its run report gives step order, limits, loop counts, pass/fail rules
Bare .vi only: lvkit describe, lvkit render (SVG drawing), lvkit unresolved. No lvkit and no export means stop and ask; do not guess
Always: a recording of one real run (CSV or TDMS) plus the raw samples that produced it. This is the contract
Invoke: /labview-to-python <path to .vi or export> <recording.csv>

slides.title: Step 4 exactly: the proof commands
bullets: python example-system/bench/rig.py --replay example-system/bench/rig_samples.csv --out outputs/rig-python.csv
python tools/bench_compare.py example-system/bench/rig_recording.csv outputs/rig-python.csv --markdown > outputs/rig-compare.md
Swap the example paths for <rig>.py, the owner's samples, and the owner's recording
Exact match for integers and verdict strings; a stated tolerance per float column, with the reason (--tol mean_temp_cc=1)
A FAIL row in the recording must stay a FAIL row in the Python; the example keeps one on purpose
PASS means the Python agrees with this recording on every compared column, not that it equals the VI everywhere. Say specification-level reconstruction until one live run matches

slides.title: LabVIEW to Python nuances the skill checks for you
bullets: Round To Nearest is ties-to-even: Python round() matches, int(x + 0.5) does not
I16 saturates, Python int does not; DBL vs SGL; NaN in Mean and Max; integer division and modulo on negatives
The error cluster becomes one exception type; try/finally where the VI had a cleanup frame
Shift registers and feedback nodes become variables that outlive the loop; local and global variables become arguments and return values
While Loop + case on an enum becomes a state machine with one function per state; producer/consumer becomes queue.Queue
Front panels and charts are not rebuilt; results go to a CSV and, if wanted, a deck
Instruments are injected functions so the same code runs live and in replay; pyvisa or pyserial only behind that seam, installed from a wheel folder offline

slides.title: Stage 4. /track-and-report: backlog status
Stage 4, when and how
bullets: The scan already wrote the backlog in tracker form: outputs/<name>-migration-backlog.json (top N capabilities, ids VI-CAP-001 ...)
Report it: python tools/tracker_report.py --file outputs/<name>-migration-backlog.json (--markdown for a document), or /track-and-report status of that file
To live in the team tracker: python tools/tracker_import.py --from csv --in outputs/<name>-migration-backlog.csv --out t.json --merge <your tracker.json> --prefix <PREFIX>
Statuses: proposed, open, in_review (port written), closed (bench_compare PASS on the owner's recording); wont_fix for rows re-classified retain
Owner is a role, never a person; component is the VI's folder; requirements and hazards link to your own IDs when you have them
Re-run the scan after each sprint with the same --name: existing items keep id, status, owner; new VIs get new ids; --fresh starts over. The report shows the burndown

slides.title: Stage 5. /exec-deck: the migration-readiness brief
Stage 5, when and how
bullets: At a milestone, when leadership needs the decision: how big the estate is, how it splits, what the first sprint proved, what is unproven
Invoke: /exec-deck Migration readiness from outputs/<name>-fleet-summary.json and outputs/<name>-fleet-report.md
Devin writes an outline JSON (like templates/deck-outline-example.json), then builds it: python tools/build_deck.py <outline.json> outputs/<name>.html
PowerPoint on request: python tools/export_pptx.py <outline.json> outputs/<name>.pptx
Every number on a slide is copied from the summary JSON, tracker_report.py, or bench_compare.py output, with a source note under the slide
Rules baked in: one idea per slide, at most 8 bullets, no organisation or person names, a footer that says the data is synthetic or public
The HTML is self-contained (no fonts, scripts, or images fetched); this deck was built the same way

slides.title: What to ask the LabVIEW owners for, in this order
bullets: A read-only copy of the project tree, .lvproj files included: targets tell the scanner what is RT or FPGA
One recording of a real run per candidate VI, plus the raw samples that produced it. Nothing else proves anything
The HTML export (File > Print > HTML) for the first sprint's VIs; screenshots per case frame where that is not possible
Passwords or unlocked copies for password-protected diagrams, or accept them as unreadable
TestStand sequences saved in the XML file format (Sequence File Properties > File Format) so their VI calls are visible
Which VIs are certified as-is: they go straight to retain regardless of what the diagram says

slides.title: Limits to state out loud
bullets: Static inventory is not runtime proof. Only bench_compare.py against a recording proves a port, and only for that recording
Nothing here runs a VI, reads FPGA or Real-Time semantics, or measures timing; those stay retain until a hardware test says otherwise
lvkit is alpha, open source, optional. It read 4 of 4 real VIs here; another estate may differ. Its generate command is not the deliverable
Classification uses names and node types; a proprietary driver named unusually will look like port until someone reads it
Everything runs locally with no network. Whether a laptop or a tool sits inside any accreditation boundary is your administrator's statement, not this repository's
The shipped example is four small VIs; the schedule for your estate comes from your first scan, not from these slides
